Do you want to work with advanced radar and RF technology used by some of the world’s top athletes? Working with our technology means creating real, tangible solutions and seeing them come to life in practice.

Join us in shaping the next generation of sports tracking systems. We operate at the intersection of radar, sensors, and computer vision, and you will have real influence on both the technology and the direction. You will be part of a highly specialized team where expertise, curiosity, and collaboration matter more than hierarchy. Decisions are fast, and ideas quickly turn into real products.

**Your role

**You will play a key role in designing and developing advanced RF and microwave solutions for our radar platforms. Your responsibilities will include:

• Taking technical lead on RF and microwave circuit design

• Contributing to next-generation radar hardware development

• Designing and optimizing components such as amplifiers, LNAs, oscillators, PLLs, mixers, and antennas (X- and K-band)

• Performing link budget and system-level calculations

• Collaborating closely with embedded software and tracking teams

• Exploring and implementing innovative technologies within RF, mmWave, and related fields

• You will have a high degree of autonomy and real influence on technical decisions.

Job requirements

We imagine that you:

• Have 5+ years of experience in RF/microwave engineering

• Have a strong theoretical foundation and can apply it in practice

• Are experienced with RF design and simulation tools

• Are comfortable using lab equipment (e.g., spectrum/network analyzers, oscilloscopes)

• Understand signal processing

It is a plus if you also have:

• Experience with Python or data analysis

• Interest in tracking or signal processing methods

• Knowledge of production or regulatory constraints

**Join us: Global impact in an inspiring workplace

**Work from one of Denmark’s most inspiring offices at our state-of-the-art Innovation Center in Hørsholm, located in DTU Science Park north of Copenhagen. Surrounded by beautiful forests, you will enjoy bright workspaces, innovative labs, on-site fitness, and a top-tier canteen serving fresh meals daily by our own chef which you can enjoy in the indoor and outdoor area.

From this unique setting, you will contribute to a truly global organization. Founded in 2003 by three Danish entrepreneurs, Trackman today has more than 1,000 employees and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul, and Tokyo. Our Innovation Center in Denmark remains at the heart of our hardware and software development, testing, and production driving impact across the world of sports technology.

One-of-a kind technology

At Trackman, we combine advanced radar, computer vision, and data to push the boundaries of sports performance. You will collaborate with talented colleagues and collaborate with leading athletes and organizations across golf, baseball, football, and other sports. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new physical and technical boundaries. Working with our technology means creating real, tangible solutions and seeing them come to life in practice.

A culture that drives innovation

We believe great products are built by great people. At Trackman, you will be part of an ambitious, entrepreneurial culture where curiosity is encouraged, ideas are shared openly, and innovation is a team effort. We foster an environment where you can challenge, make your voice heard, and help shape solutions that set new standards in sports technology for a better game.

Company Description

At Coach Solutions, we build software that helps the global shipping industry work smarter and make data-driven decisions — for both profit and sustainability. Backed by Kongsberg Maritime, we're entering a new phase: modernizing our architecture and scaling our impact.

Job Description

We're looking for a Senior Frontend / Full-Stack Developer to join our Platform & Development department. You'll take ownership of frontend development across our SaaS products, working closely with developers, QA, Product, and other stakeholders to deliver reliable, scalable software used by customers across the shipping industry.

Our stack centres on Next.js, React, Typescript and Vercel, backed by Azure and .NET Standard services, with Mapbox and tilesets powering our geospatial visualizations. We're an AI-fluent team — you'll be expected to use AI-assisted tools as part of how you work, not just be curious about them.

Qualifications

What you'll do

• Design, build, and maintain modern frontend applications with React and Next.js.

• Build interactive maps and geospatial visualizations using Mapbox and tilesets.

• Integrate frontend applications with backend REST APIs, including .NET Standard services — with room to grow into full-stack work overtime.

• Contribute to modernizing our existing architecture, with an eye on maintainability, scalability, and security.

• Own features end-to-end: from design and implementation through testing, deployment, and monitoring (via tools like Monitive).

• Use GitHub and GitHub Actions for version control, code review, and CI/CD.

• Use AI-assisted development tools day-to-day to improve code quality, testing, and delivery speed.

• Share knowledge, raise technical risks early, and help shape how the team works.

What you bring

Must have

• 5+ years of professional software development experience, with a strong focus on frontend and production software used by real customers.

• Strong hands-on experience with React, Next.js, and TypeScript/JavaScript.

• Solid grasp of frontend architecture: component design, state management, responsive UIs.

• Experience integrating frontend apps with REST APIs and backend services.

• Comfortable with Git/GitHub, code review, and CI/CD pipelines.

• Genuinely AI-fluent: you already use AI coding tools and understand their limits, not just open to trying them.

• Clear communicator — able to explain technical trade-offs to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders.

Nice to have (we'll teach the rest)

• Experience with Mapbox, tilesets, or geospatial data — no prior background required if you're keen to learn.

• Exposure to Vercel deployment workflows.

• Comfort working in Azure-based environments.

• .NET Standard experience, or interest in growing into full-stack work.

• Familiarity with monitoring/observability tools such as Monitive.

Additional Information

Practical details

• Location: Copenhagen, on-site with hybrid flexibility

• Team: Platform & Development department

Why Coach Solutions

• A purpose-driven workplace at the intersection of tech and sustainability.

• Real influence: if you see the problem, you own it — and if you make the best argument, you win, regardless of title.

• An informal, social culture — monthly Friday bars, team events, summer and winter parties, family events, and more.

• A skilled mentor and an experienced, engineering-minded team eager to help you succeed.

• Room to grow — new responsibilities and career paths as the company scales.

Don't check every box?

That's okay — we'd still love to hear from you. If you have strong frontend experience, a passion for building great software, and the motivation to learn and grow, reach out. Let's build something meaningful together.

jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Civil and Architectural Engineering programme. The position is available from 1 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
AI-augmented Physiological Modelling for Prediction and Mitigation of Heat Stress in Pigs

Research area and project description:
Heat stress is an increasing challenge to pig production and animal welfare, particularly during hot seasons. Effective mitigation requires not only the detection of elevated heat load, but also the ability to predict how animals respond dynamically and to determine when and how cooling interventions should be applied. Existing mechanistic thermal models provide an important basis for representing animal heat balance and physiological responses. However, their ability to incorporate real-time physiological observations, account for model assumptions and environmental stochasticity, and support timely intervention decisions remains limited. At the same time, purely data-driven black-box approaches are challenging to develop and validate when high-quality physiological datasets are limited, as is often the case in controlled animal experiments.

This PhD project aims to develop a physics-informed digital model for predicting and mitigating heat stress in pigs. Building on conventional mechanistic models of pig physiological responses, the project will investigate how physiological modelling can be combined with AI approaches to develop a more robust and interpretable representation of the pig’s thermal state. To further enhance the accessibility and practical use of the model, the project will also explore how large language models (LLMs) can be integrated with the physiological model to facilitate interactive exploration of model behaviour and predictions.

Qualifications and specific competences:
We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with:
• A MSc degree in Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, or Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or related filed.
• A strong academic background and interest in HVAC systems in buildings, and fluid and thermal systems modelling.
• Proven experience in data analytics, machine learning, and optimisation.
• Ability to program using Python, R, MATLAB or similar platforms.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in interdisciplinary teams.
• Excellent written and spoken English skills.It is considered an advantage if you have:
• Knowledge of animal heat stress and animal welfare.
• Knowledge of Large Language Model, stochastic modelling, system identification.
• Experience with CFD simulations.
Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering, Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, 8000 Aarhus C., Denmark.

Contacts:
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
• Associate Professor Li Rong, e-mail: li.rong@cae.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Assistant Professor Tao Huang, e-mail: taoh@cae.au.dk (co-supervisor)For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk

Do you want to join a global fund manager in energy infrastructure investments? If so, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) is currently looking for an Analyst to join our Global Rewards team based in Copenhagen.

Team

The Global Rewards Team is part of the broader People team at CIP and is responsible for designing and delivering CIP's global reward framework, ensuring our compensation, benefits, mobility, and incentive programs support both our business strategy and employee value proposition. As a trusted partner to senior leaders and stakeholders across the organization, the team develops scalable and market-leading reward solutions that enable us to attract, retain, and motivate top talent globally.

The team works at the intersection of People, Finance, and business leadership, providing strategic guidance on compensation structures, incentive programs, global mobility, benefits, job architecture, and pay transparency. Through a combination of analytical rigor, commercial insight, and close stakeholder collaboration, the team helps shape a rewarding and high-performance culture across CIP's global platform.

Role

We are looking for a curious, analytical, and detail-oriented Student Assistant to join our Incentives function within the Global Rewards team. This is a great opportunity for a student interested in gaining practical experience working with incentives programs.

As our Student Analyst, you will support incentives activities across multiple countries on both operational and strategic initiatives.

The position is part-time (around 20 hours per week) and based in our headquarters in NordØ. The workload will vary depending on ongoing projects, with flexibility to structure your time according to your schedule.

Responsibilities will consist of but are not limited to:

• Support onboarding new employees in our Long-Term Programs, i.e. handling and sending out Transfer Notes, Shareholder Agreements, Tax Side Letters to our employees and provide overall legal information of the content such as leaver terms, vesting conditions and maintaining all relevant data in our systems.

• Exit employees from our Long-Term Programs whenever we have leavers.

• Supporting our stakeholders by keeping an overview of employees enrolled in different programs.

• Ad hoc support when we create new Long-Term Programs or enter new markets to accommodate business needs.

• Assist employees with Long-Term Incentive matters, e.g. answer questions regarding eligibility, rights, tax implications, etc.

• Drive projects supporting employees with Long-Term Incentives.

You

You are ideally in 2-3 years of your Bachelor’s or 1st year of Master’s pursuing a degree in Commercial Law and Business Administration or similar. You enjoy working in a busy and collaborative environment, taking responsibility for your own projects, and driving them forward with confidence and independence. Having relevant experience is beneficial.

We look for the following in the candidate:

• A proactive and curious mindset, combined with a strong willingness to learn and develop. You take ownership of your work, seek continuous improvement, and thrive in an environment that offers new challenges and learning opportunities.

• Highly detail-oriented and structured in your approach, with the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining a high level of accuracy. You handle confidential and sensitive information with professionalism, discretion, and integrity.

• You are confident using PowerPoint to transform data and insights into clear and impactful presentations for a range of stakeholders and have good Excel skills.

• Professional written and verbal communication skills in English, enabling you to communicate effectively and build strong relationships with stakeholders across a global organization.

Please note that we do not offer a remote working opportunity, thus you must be a Danish resident or an upcoming student enrolled in a Danish university to be eligible for this role. Students on exchange in Denmark are not considered eligible for this position.

The process

Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

---

Building value that matters

Founded in 2012, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners P/S (CIP) today is the world’s largest dedicated fund manager within greenfield renewable energy investments and a global leader in offshore wind. To date, CIP has developed and constructed more than +50 greenfield renewable projects around the world. CIP is developing a greenfield project portfolio of ~160GW total, and ~16 GW is in operation or under construction. CIP manages 13 funds and has to date raised approximately EUR ~35 billion for investments in energy and associated infrastructure from more than ~200 international institutional investors.

CIP has a multinational team of ~500 full-time employees with extensive experience and knowledge within the fields of renewable energy project development and regulated infrastructure. In addition, CIP has a broad range of competencies within corporate finance, mergers & acquisitions, engineering, construction, project development, and project management.

CIP has built a prominent investment team capable of originating proprietary investment opportunities and executing projects and investments based on the team’s industrial background, large industrial network, and extensive experience in structuring, executing, and managing investments within energy infrastructure. Headquartered in Copenhagen, CIP also operates from key locations across the globe, including offices in Hamburg, Munich, London, Utrecht, New York, Tokyo, Melbourne, Luxembourg, Kuala Lumpur, Seoul and Singapore. In addition, CIP has 17 local project offices globally.

Senior Finance Business Partner, Commercial Performance Europe

Location: Gentofte, Denmark or Lisbon, Portugal

Working hours: Full-time

Work model: Hybrid

Contract type: Permanent

Are you passionate about turning commercial performance into strategic business value? Do you want to influence key decisions, drive profitability, and help shape the future of a leading international business? Then you might be the person we are looking for.

You will work closely with Sales, Marketing, Category Management, Operations, and Finance leaders to translate commercial strategy into measurable financial outcomes. This is an exciting opportunity to influence strategic decisions, support the delivery of our Focus2030 ambitions, and strengthen value creation across multiple European markets.

What your day will look like

In this role, you will typically focus on:

• Leading the financial performance management of the European business, creating a clear and consolidated view of commercial results and key value drivers.

ACCSION is Aalborg Portland’s project to build Denmark’s largest facility to capture and store CO2, making the plant carbon neutral on its own emissions.

Working closely with the Project Director, PMO, workstream leads, and Value Chain Partners, you will help ensure that the programme is effectively planned, controlled, and reported. You will bring together project information, identify risks and deviations, and turn complex data into clear insights that support good management decisions.

A central part of the role will be developing and continuously improving the project controls framework for ACCSION. This includes planning and scheduling, KPIs, forecasting, reporting, governance, and standardised processes across the programme and its partners.

You will also be responsible for ensuring that project information is well organised, traceable, and audit-ready. This includes maintaining document structures and version control, as well as supporting documentation related to funding, subsidies, procurement, contracts, tenders, and key project decisions.

In this role, you will

• 
Establish and maintain project plans, schedules, milestones, KPIs, forecasts, and management reporting.

• 
Provide the Project Director and leadership team with analysis and decision-support information.

• 
Identify risks, deviations, trends, and opportunities for improvement.

• 
Develop and standardise project controls, governance processes, reporting structures, and management tools.

• 
Coordinate information and reporting across workstreams, internal teams, and Value Chain Partners.

• 
Maintain robust document control and ensure a clear audit trail across the programme.

• 
Support the PMO and workstreams in meeting governance, reporting, and documentation requirements.

About you

You are a structured and analytical project professional who enjoys bringing clarity to complex projects. You have an eye for detail but also understand the bigger picture and what management needs to make informed decisions.

You bring:

• 
A relevant degree in engineering, project management, finance, or a related field.

• 
5+ years of experience in Project Controls, PMO, or large-scale technical projects.

• 
Strong experience with planning, scheduling, forecasting, risk, change, cost, and management reporting.

• 
Experience developing project controls or governance frameworks.

• 
Proficiency with Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or similar tools.

• 
Experience from large EPC, engineering, infrastructure, or industrial projects is an advantage.

• 
Excellent written and spoken business-level English.

• 
PMP, IPMA, or equivalent certification is an advantage.

Most importantly, you are someone who takes ownership, creates structure, and is comfortable working across different teams and organisations. You communicate clearly, challenge when needed, and are motivated by making complex projects more transparent and manageable.

**We offer

**We offer an ambitious, international and professional workplace that, with its high level of professionalism, continually focuses on the employees' professional and personal development through structured development interviews. For the right candidates, there are also many internal career opportunities. We are an informal workplace with a focus on close collaboration, knowledge sharing and free dialogue. In addition, we have a working environment characterized by freedom with responsibility and flexibility.

**Employment

**This is a 12-month fixed-term position covering maternity leave, with employment starting as soon as possible.

**How to apply

**If the position sounds interesting, please send your application and CV. We would like to point out that interviews will be held on an ongoing basis, and therefore we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close the recruitment once the right candidate has been found. Employment will start as soon as possible.

You can get further information about the position from our Group Sustainability Director, Jesper Sand Damtoft by phone +45 4018 1121.

**More about us

**The position is located at the Cementir Holding Research and Quality Centre, located in Aalborg. Since 2004, Aalborg Portland has been part of the Cementir Group. The Nordic & Baltic Region of the Cementir Group comprises four business units, with Aalborg Portland A/S as the largest and other ready mixed concrete and aggregates businesses under Unicon A/S in Denmark, Unicon AS in Norway, and AB Sydsten in Sweden.

Aalborg Portland is Europe’s largest cement plant, operating seven kiln lines and a unique dock facility with direct access to global logistics. With raw material resources located in immediate proximity and a distribution network of nine terminals across Denmark and Northern Europe, Aalborg Portland serves customers throughout Europe, with its primary market in Scandinavia. Denmark remains the strongest market, where the company holds more than 90% market share. They have around 300 dedicated employees.

Aalborg Portland is also leading the industry’s green transition being ‘Part of the Solution’ ! Under the project name ACCSION, the company plans to capture and store 1.4 million tonnes of CO₂ per year and enable the production of cement types with an ultralow CO₂ footprint.

Aalborg Portland Nordic & Baltic offers equal opportunities for all and have an active focus on fostering a work environment that is free from discrimination and where employees are treated with dignity and respect. In our company employment is based on an individual's merit and qualifications, which are directly related to job competence. We do not discriminate against any employee or job applicant based on race, ethnicity, nationality, ancestry, genetic information, citizenship, religion, age, gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, marital status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, rules or regulations. We adhere to these principles in all aspects of employment, including recruiting, hiring, training, compensation, promotion, and benefits.

jobs.description:
PhD position in Compilation Principles for Reversible Languages (MSCA Doctoral Network E-CoRe, DC7), University of Copenhagen
 
 The position is doctoral candidate DC7, “Compilation Principles for Reversible Languages", in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network E-CoRe. The position is available from 1 January 2027, or after agreement.
 
 Job description
 The Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section, part of the Department of Computer Science (DIKU), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for a 3-year PhD position on compilation principles for reversible languages.
 
 The project
 The position is funded by the European Union under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks (MSCA-DN) programme, grant agreement no. 101120187. The project advances the science and practice of reversible computing for a sustainable digital future. Energy is a main concern in society: IT accounts for an estimated 10% of global energy consumption. Reversible computation discards no information and therefore avoids the fundamental energy lower bound of conventional computing. The network trains a cohort of doctoral candidates who will improve and popularise reversible languages, algorithms, and architectures for energy-intensive applications. 

  Read more about the network at https://e-core.nws.cs.unibo.it/.
 
 The position is open for talented candidates with a master’s degree, who want to pursue a PhD degree in Computer Science.

  DC7: The successful PhD candidate will work on compilation principles and techniques for reversible languages. The candidate can build on the work by project members. 

  Concretely, the work includes the following:

   	
• Studying techniques for translating high-level reversible languages into efficient low-level reversible and irreversible representations. 	
• Designing optimisation techniques for reversible languages, including foundational methods and novel approaches to program analysis and code generation. 	
• Implementing prototype compilers to evaluate optimisation techniques, alongside a benchmark suite specifically designed for reversible compilation and empirical evaluation. 	
• Publishing the results at international conferences and in peer-reviewed journals.   Planned Secondments: Technische Hochschule Mittelhessen (Germany), University of Manchester (UK).

  Key criteria for the assessment of applicants for the position:  

  The candidate must have a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish Master's degree) in Computer Science or a closely related field, obtained by the recruitment date.

  Certified copy of original Master of Science diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in a language other than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.

  As a prerequisite for a PhD fellowship employment, your master’s degree must be equivalent to a Danish master’s degree. We encourage you to read more in the assessment database: https://ufsn.dk/english/education/recognition-and-transparency/find-assessments/assessment-database/ 

  Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science.

  Other important criteria are:

   	
• Strong academic record and motivation for doctoral research.  	
• Experience in compiler design, program analysis, and language semantics, regardless of programming paradigm, is an advantage. Prior knowledge of reversible computing is not needed. 	
• Ability to work independently, take initiative, and collaborate effectively in an international research environment. Proactive and team-oriented approach to work. 	
• Proficiency in written and spoken English. 	
• Willingness and ability to travel and undertake secondments at other project partners.   The successful candidate will be employed as a PhD student at the Department of Computer Science at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Copenhagen, and will collaborate closely with the group at the University of Southern Denmark, Odense, which is also an E-CoRe partner. The position may involve co-supervising related student projects. The PhD student is expected to participate in the activities of the research section and in the training programme of the E-CoRe network.
 The main supervisor is Professor Robert Glück (e-mail: glueck@di.ku.dk), whose current research focus is on programming languages, reversible computing, program generation, and metaprogramming.

  Start date:    1 January 2027, or after agreement with the cohort of the MSCA-DN

  Duration:      3 years

  The successful candidate will conduct independent research related to the topics above at the Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section, Department of Computer Science (DIKU). We expect the candidate to engage in an active research environment and take part in student guidance.

  Note: Another job opening for DC1 “Reversible Programming Languages” is available. More information: XXX-LINK-TO-DC1.
 
 Mobility rule
 The researcher must not have resided or carried out his/her/their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately before the recruitment date. Short stays as holidays and compulsory military service and/or Refugee Convention 1951 are disregarded.

  Eligibility as Doctoral Candidate (DC)
 The recruited DC must be doctoral candidate, i.e. not already in possession of a doctoral degree on the first day of employment. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree will not be considered eligible.
 
 Workplace description 
 The Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section is part of the Department of Computer Science (DIKU) at the Faculty of Science, located on the North Campus in Copenhagen. At the section we research topics such as algorithmic aspects of programming, compiler technology, functional programming, reversible and quantum computing. You will be part of an international group of PhD students, postdocs, and faculty working at the intersection of programming languages, theory of computing, and various applications.

  More information about PLTC and DIKU can be found at https://di.ku.dk/english/research/pltc/  and https://di.ku.dk/english/.

  Terms of employment 
 Salary, pension and terms of employment will be in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organization. Currently, the monthly salary starts at DKK 31,845 / approx. EUR 4,260 (August 2026-level). 
 Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.
 
 The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  Further information
 For further information, please contact Professor Robert Glück (e-mail: glueck@di.ku.dk).

  International applicants may find this link useful: https://ism.ku.dk/ (International Staff Mobility) or https://www.workindenmark.dk/.

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• Master of Science diploma and transcript of records. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor will do. 	
• Publication list (if any).   Deadline for applications: Sunday 1 November 2026, 23:59 PM CET.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee which will consist of both internal (UCPH) and external members. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed, each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You may read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.
 
 The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.
